q1.answer: 18/18 Class-A failures lose their last legal EXIT placement before EXIT first appears. In 17/18 the persistent positive-to-zero transition occurs 1-18 completed turns before first sighting; in seed 2001 it occurs on the action whose post-action draw first reveals EXIT, so the board loses capacity before the draw within that canonical action. Capacity is zero at first sighting in all 18.

q2.answer: Capacity is not absorbing in general: 10/18 Class-A trajectories recover from at least one earlier zero-capacity interval before EXIT sighting. However all 18 later suffer a persistent last-slot loss; after that persistent loss, 0/18 recover before sighting or while EXIT is visible, and all 18 remain continuously zero whenever EXIT is visible.

q3.answer: At the 18 first-sighting states, 76 frontier-attached EXIT candidates were examined and all were illegal. The exact engine reasons were 74 'only a visible water cell may be covered' and 2 'tunnel/earth mismatch with adjacent card'. Candidate-coordinate provenance shows the 74 overlap failures have an empty connectable frontier cell and an occupied terminal EXIT half, so 16/18 sighting states are terminal_cell_space_blocked and 2/18 are mixed_geometry_block. Terminal-half space blockage is therefore the dominant geometric rule.

q4.answer: At the first last-slot-killing decision, all 18/18 Class-A seeds have at least one legal capacity-preserving alternative and 0/18 are locally unavoidable. Three preserving alternatives are already tied in the actual global-best set; the other 15 score lower. Exact first-loss score gaps are 0-300 (median 100, mean 125). The later persistent loss is also avoidable in all 18; 17/18 persistent gaps are <=300, with one 22,000-point outlier driven by current water-cover/water-space scoring.

q5.answer: Successful V4 trajectories do not uniformly preserve capacity. Five of 14 canonical wins (2005, 2238, 2282, 2286, 2371) pass through capacity=0 before EXIT placement, and all five recover. Seed 2371 even has zero capacity at first EXIT sighting and later recovers to place EXIT and win. The other 13/14 are positive at sighting, and 13/14 stay positive continuously from sighting to placement. Each of the five winner last-slot kills has a capacity-preserving alternative (gap 100-250), so the proposed unconditional guard would directly change five canonical winning trajectories.

rationale: The Class-A failure mechanism is real: all 18 are zero-capacity at EXIT sighting and all 18 have a locally avoidable persistent last-slot loss.
But zero capacity is not an absorbing bad state: 10/18 Class-A seeds recover from earlier zero intervals before their later persistent loss.
Five of 14 canonical V4 wins also pass through zero capacity and recover; one winning seed (2371) is zero at EXIT first sighting.

All five winner last-slot kills have feasible preserving alternatives, so the proposed unconditional last-slot guard would alter canonical winning behavior rather than merely removing a failure-specific action.
Class-C controls place EXIT immediately with positive capacity and still later dead-end, confirming EXIT access alone is not sufficient.

capacity_metric_semantics.capacity_is_diagnostic_only: EXIT is never inserted into the canonical hand; capacity uses only the visible board and public EXIT geometry.
capacity_metric_semantics.exit_compatible_frontier_target_count: Across legal EXIT moves, count distinct board open_tunnel_target_counts coordinates occupied by the rotated EXIT cell carrying its sole external tunnel edge. Equivalent moves attaching at the same frontier cell count once.
capacity_metric_semantics.exit_legal_move_count: len(legal_moves(board, (canonical_exit_card,))); uses canonical move generation and Board.can_place.
capacity_metric_semantics.zero_interval: Consecutive distinct action-state turns with exit_legal_move_count == 0 before EXIT placement. Refreshes do not change board state or create a new action-state turn.

recommended_next_step: Authorize exactly one bounded, non-mutating reversibility-discriminator audit on these same spent last-slot-killing states: compare the 18 persistent Class-A losses against all naturally recovering zero-capacity transitions in Class A and the 5 canonical winning trajectories, and determine whether any existing visible-state geometric property distinguishes persistent terminal-space closure from reversible zero-capacity dips. Do not implement a guard or V5 and do not continue counterfactual trajectories.
unresolved_risks: All evidence is already-spent diagnostic data; no population win-rate or holdout inference is justified.
A capacity-preserving alternative was evaluated only locally at a fixed historical state; no alternative trajectory was continued.

The proposed strict guard is falsified as failure-specific by reversible zero-capacity transitions in 5/14 canonical wins, but this audit does not establish whether a narrower persistent-loss discriminator exists.
Class-C controls show that preserving EXIT access cannot by itself guarantee victory after EXIT placement.
